data.name: Fantasynth One
data.detailed_description:
Fantasynth One is an audio-reactive experience designed for Virtual Reality.

Glide through a procedurally populated environment that comes alight with the music.

Official Selection SIGGRAPH Animation Festival 2017.

Featuring the song Chez Nous by N'to, published by Hungry Music.

Duration: 7 minutes.

reviews.review:
Fantasynth One is a very short VR experience that is basically built around music, movement and visuals rather than traditional gameplay. I am placed inside a colourful abstract world and glide through it while the environment reacts to the electronic music playing around me. There are no enemies to fight, no puzzles to solve and no real objectives to worry about. It is more like stepping into a music video and being able to move through it myself. That simple idea works surprisingly well when I just want something relaxing and visually interesting.

The visuals are easily the strongest part for me. The world is filled with glowing shapes, strange structures and constantly changing colours, and everything moves in time with the music. Because the environment is procedurally populated, the experience feels like it is constantly flowing forward instead of taking me through a normal set of levels. I like how the scenery and music work together because neither one feels completely separate from the other. The whole thing has a very futuristic feeling that suits VR extremely well.

The music is also important because there is only one main track, Chez Nous by N'to, and the environment is built around it. I actually think the choice to focus on one track makes sense for what Fantasynth One is trying to do. I am not distracted by menus, dialogue or other systems and can simply sit back and experience the music with the visuals. The movement is smooth and more about gliding through the world than actively controlling a complicated vehicle, which helps keep the experience calm.

The biggest problem is obviously the length. The complete experience is around seven minutes, so I can see almost everything in one sitting. That is extremely short even for a free experimental game. I can replay it if I want to enjoy the visuals and music again, but there is no real progression or reason for me to keep coming back once I have experienced it properly. I think the quality of those few minutes is good enough to make the experience worthwhile, but I cannot ignore how little actual content there is.

I also think the VR requirement limits how useful the game is for me. This is designed specifically for virtual reality and SteamVR, so I cannot treat it like a normal desktop game that I can quickly launch whenever I want. When I have the right setup, the VR format makes much more sense because the feeling of moving through the environment is part of what makes it interesting. Without that, there is not really much of a game left underneath the visuals and music.

There are some signs that the age of the experience is starting to show as well. Fantasynth One originally released in 2017, and while the abstract visuals still look good, the whole thing feels more like an early VR showcase than a complete modern game. That is not necessarily a criticism because I think it succeeds at being a showcase. I just have to judge it for what it actually offers rather than giving it credit for systems it simply does not have. It is an experience rather than something I would sit down and play for hours.

Overall, I think Fantasynth One is worth experiencing if I have VR and want something short, relaxing and visually impressive. The music works well with the audio reactive environment, the abstract visuals are memorable and the smooth movement makes the whole thing easy to enjoy. The seven minute length and complete lack of traditional gameplay stop me from giving it a really high score, but it is also completely free, so I do not feel like I am being asked to make a big commitment. For me, it is a neat little VR experience that does exactly what it sets out to do, even if that goal only lasts for a few minutes.

Rating: 7.4/10
